blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Feed-forward 3D models use Transformers to predict camera poses, depth, and structure in one pass, avoiding iterative multi-view optimization. Long sequences and deep attention incur high compute and memory costs, motivating Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) for deployment. Existing PTQ methods mainly suppress channel-wise outliers by smoothing or orthogonal rotation. Geometry Transformers introduce a different challenge: heterogeneous token types share one activation quantization grid. A few special tokens may exert high leverage over global outputs and be updated by only a subset of blocks. Token-blind transforms, which apply the same transformation to every token, reduce overall quantization error but cannot remove differentiated degradation across token types. We propose QMapAnything, a structure-aware PTQ framework. We cast floating-point-preserving rotation and smoothing as a token-blind reparameterization group, and prove that they yield common-mode gains while leaving relative token SNR unchanged. We introduce a statistic $Γ$ that combines a special token's quantization disadvantage and output leverage to predict whether differentiated bias correction is needed beyond rotation. Experiments on geometric benchmarks show that W4A8 closely matches full-precision performance. Under W8A8, peak memory falls by $2.2$--$3.1\times$ versus FP32, with up to $3.1\times$ speedup on real hardware. These results provide a principled and efficient approach to deploying feed-forward 3D reconstruction models in resource-constrained edges.
blocks.zh: Feed-forward 3D模型使用变形器在一次通过中预测相机的姿势,深度,结构,避免迭代多视图优化. 长时间的序列和深度的注意需要高昂的计算和内存成本,促使训练后量化(PTQ)进行部署. 现有的PTQ方法主要通过平滑或正交旋转来压制信道的偏转器. 几何变形器引入了不同的挑战:多种符号类型共享一个激活量化网格. 少数特殊标志可能对全球产出产生很大影响,仅通过一组区块加以更新。 Token-blind变换,将相同的变换应用到每一个符,减少整体的量化错误,但不能消除各种符号类型的不同降解. 我们提出QMapAnything,一个结构意识的PTQ框架. 我们把浮点保持旋转和平滑作为标志性盲光再参数化组,并证明它们能产生共同模式收益,同时保持相对符号SNR不变。 我们采用了一种统计性美元,将特殊标志的量化劣势和产出杠杆结合起来,预测在轮换之外是否需要有区别的偏差纠正。 对几何基准的实验表明,W4A8与全精度性能紧密匹配. 在W8A8下,峰值内存与FP32相比下降了2.2美元-3.1美元/时,实际硬件的速率高达3.1美元/时. 这些成果为在受资源制约的边缘地区部署向前进的三维重建模式提供了一个原则性和高效率的方法。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Classical multi-view reconstruction combines geometric priors with iterative
optimization ( Mur-Artal and Tardós, 2017 ; Schönberger and Frahm, 2016 ; Schönberger et al., 2016 ) . Learning-based systems first moved dense
matching and point-map prediction into neural networks ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Leroy et al., 2024 ) , and recent
feed-forward Transformers now recover camera pose, depth, and 3D structure jointly in a single
forward pass ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Keetha et al., 2026 ) . This paradigm offers strong generalization without
per-scene optimization, but its long token sequences and deep attention stacks impose substantial
memory and computation costs, making post-training quantization (PTQ) attractive for deployment.

blocks.en:
Recent PTQ methods suppress outliers through scaling, smoothing, or orthogonal
rotation ( Xiao et al., 2023 ; Ashkboos et al., 2024 ; Tseng et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025 ) . Related recipes have been extended
to visual geometry Transformers ( Feng et al., 2026 ; Pan et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ) . These methods act along the
channel axis, whereas feed-forward geometry models can be asymmetric along the token axis. We
identify four properties that characterize this mismatch: (S1) heterogeneous token types
share one activation grid. (S2) A single token has multiplicative, output-wide leverage. (S3) Channel energy is heavy-tailed. (S4) The special token
is updated by only a subset of blocks. Rotation addresses S3, but its token-blind action
cannot remove the differentiated error created by S1–S2. Consequently, metric outputs may fail
even when scale-aligned geometry remains plausible, and a recipe successful on an up-to-scale
model need not transfer to a metric one.

blocks.en:
We present QMapAnything, a structure-aware PTQ framework that uses these properties to select mechanisms.
We first characterize all floating-point-preserving rotation and smoothing transformations as a
token-blind reparameterization group. Orthogonal transformations provide a common-mode signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain but
leave relative token SNR unchanged. More general transformations face a conditioning ceiling and a
potential weight-side quantization trade-off. We then introduce Γ \Gamma , a screening statistic that combines a
token’s grid disadvantage with its output leverage. It requires only one forward and
backward pass per scene and screens for the need for token-selective treatment. A residual statistic measured
during calibration determines affine correctability. Guided by this analysis, QMapAnything pairs a
rotation matrix for S3 with standard bias correction and, where warranted,
a row-selective affine correction for S1–S2, inserted only where S4 makes it necessary. MapAnything
provides the primary stress test, while Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) and Depth Anything 3 (DA3) provide complementary transfer cases. VGGT has high gradient leverage
on its special token without a grid disadvantage, whereas DA3 has a grid disadvantage without effective
output leverage.
Our contributions are summarized as follows: 1. We identify four structural properties (S1–S4) that
explain when channel-oriented PTQ transfers to a geometry Transformer and when it does not,
separating metric predictors from up-to-scale ones. 2. We prove that floating-point-preserving rotation and smoothing form a token-blind
group. They act identically on every token, so they have common-mode strength but no
row-indexed freedom. QMapAnything keeps a rotation inside this group and adds a row-selective
affine correction outside it, inserted only where S4 indicates. 3. We introduce a screening statistic for that need and a residual statistic to test affine
correctability. The former distinguishes MapAnything from VGGT and DA3, and QMapAnything attains
near-lossless low-bit accuracy with 3.1 × 3.1\times lower peak memory.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Classical pipelines separate structure-from-motion and multi-view stereo (MVS) ( Mur-Artal and Tardós, 2017 ; Schönberger and Frahm, 2016 ; Schönberger et al., 2016 ) .
Learned MVS ( Yao et al., 2018 ) and cross-view pretraining ( Weinzaepfel et al., 2022 ) move geometry into networks.
DUSt3R and MASt3R predict pairwise geometry ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Leroy et al., 2024 ) , VGGT jointly predicts pose and dense
geometry ( Wang et al., 2025 ) , and MapAnything factors metric geometry into an up-to-scale representation
and one global scale ( Keetha et al., 2026 ) . Beyond their differing prediction targets, these models
also differ in whether a special token is routed through every block and whether it multiplies
rather than merely summarizes the output. Those differences drive our analysis.

blocks.en: Table 1: Camera pose estimation, averaged over ETH3D, SN++v2 and TAV2.
blocks.zh: 表1:相机呈现出估计值,平均值为ETH3D,SN++v2和TAV2.

blocks.en:
We conduct camera pose estimation experiments on ETH3D, SN++v2, and TAV2 using 2, 8, and 16 input
views, and report AUC@30 ∘ macro-averaged over the three datasets. This metric jointly measures
relative rotation and translation accuracy. Notably, ETH3D is excluded from calibration and
therefore also evaluates cross-dataset generalization. Under the relatively moderate W4A8 setting,
QMapAnything preserves camera pose accuracy with near-lossless performance. Under the more aggressive
W4A4 setting, its gap to full precision grows progressively with the number of input views. This
trend agrees with S1. As the view count increases, more patch tokens compete to determine the shared
absmax, further reducing the effective quantization resolution of the distinguished pathway. The
ordering among baselines further validates our mechanism analysis. RTN and SmoothQuant do not
adequately address the heavy-tailed channel distribution in S3 and therefore fail to recover the
dominant common-mode loss. QuaRot substantially reduces the overall quantization error through
orthogonal rotation, but its token-blind transformation cannot alter the relative SNR between
special and patch tokens. The additional improvement of QMapAnything thus stems from explicitly
correcting differentiated errors along the token axis, rather than from dataset-specific tuning or
mismatched quantization settings.

To test generality, we further audit VGGT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) and DA3 ( Lin et al., 2026 ) , neither of which informed our method design, against S1–S4 and compute Γ \Gamma on their full-precision checkpoints. All three models share the same signed quantizer,

setting. MapAnything additionally uses a staged 40-step refinement, whereas
VGGT and DA3 use closed-form correction without gradient refinement. No accuracy-driven tuning is
performed on either transfer model. Although the audit prescribes omitting b s b_{\mathrm{s}} on VGGT and DA3, we deliberately instantiate the full B B as a conservative falsification test.
All three models satisfy S1 and S3. They use per-tensor activation scales, and their within-token max / 99 \max/99 th-percentile ( P99 \mathrm{P99} ) ratios at the final residual are substantially above the reference value for a

so it is neither multiplicatively load-bearing nor sparsely routed. DA3 introduces a camera token,
but its intermediate-layer interface removes that token before the dense head. The evaluated pose
pathway instead regresses from dense rays, leaving the token with no effective output leverage.
